name: Ancient Egyptian religion
title: The story of ancient Egyptian religion

text: More than 5,000 years ago, the land of Egypt along the Nile was joined under one king.
The Egyptians believed their king was the living Horus, a falcon god.
src: When the land was united under a single king around 3100 BCE / the farming communities of the Nile valley
The king was the living Horus / the falcon Horus

text: The Egyptians worshipped hundreds of gods, shown as people, as animals or as a mix of both.
In their stories, the god Osiris was killed by his brother Seth, brought back by Isis, and became ruler of the dead.
src: The Egyptians worshipped hundreds of gods, the netjeru, who could take human, animal or mixed forms
the god Osiris, a king murdered by his brother Seth and restored to life by his sister and wife Isis / Osiris became ruler of the realm of the dead

text: They believed in maat, the right order of the world, kept by everyone who lived fairly.
Temple walls, like those at Edfu, still show their rituals, festivals and stories.
src: The central idea of Egyptian religion was maat: truth, justice and the right order of the world / by every person who lived justly
The temples of the Ptolemaic period, at Edfu, Dendera and Philae, preserve on their walls the most complete records of temple rituals, festivals and myths

text: A temple was the house of a god, whose statue lived in a dark room at its heart.
Every morning, priests woke, washed, dressed and fed the god.
src: The temple was the house of the god, whose statue lived in a dark sanctuary at its heart
Every morning priests opened the shrine, woke, washed, clothed and fed the god with offerings

text: The Egyptians hoped to live forever, so they kept the bodies of the dead safe as mummies.
The Great Pyramid was built as the tomb of a king named Khufu.
src: Every dead person hoped to become an Osiris and to live forever / The body had to be preserved by mummification
The Great Pyramid is built at Giza as the tomb of the king Khufu

text: As Christianity spread, the old faith faded, and the last temple, of Isis at Philae, closed more than 1,400 years ago.
Its pyramids and temples, built for the gods and for life after death, remain.
src: faded with the rise of Christianity / Officials of the emperor Justinian close the temple of Isis at Philae
Ancient Egyptian religion left the most spectacular monuments of the ancient world / all built for the gods and the afterlife
